data.title: Pyoderma faciale (rosacea fulminans) — viva
data.summary: Acne & appendageal disorders · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pyoderma faciale (rosacea fulminans)** (Acne & appendageal disorders)_

**Q1. What is rosacea fulminans (pyoderma faciale)?**
- Sudden, severe, explosive variant of rosacea in young women (20–40 y) with confluent nodules, pustules, abscesses and draining sinuses on the central face on a background of intense erythema; no comedones; usually no systemic symptoms (unlike acne fulminans)

**Q2. Triggers / associations.**
- Pregnancy, emotional stress, OCP/ hormonal changes, inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's, UC), high-dose vitamin B6/B12, interferon/EGFR inhibitors, history of mild rosacea/flushing

**Q3. Clinical features.**
- Rapid-onset (days–weeks) painful, coalescing papules, pustules and fluctuant nodules on cheeks, chin, forehead, nose; marked erythema/oedema; may scar
- Fever or arthralgia are uncommon (consider acne fulminans or neutrophilic dermatosis if present)

**Q4. Classify neutrophilic dermatoses (PYQ).**
- Sweet syndrome, pyoderma gangrenosum, Behçet's, neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis, subcorneal pustular dermatosis, bowel-associated dermatosis–arthritis syndrome, rheumatoid neutrophilic dermatitis, erythema elevatum diutinum, neutrophilic dermatosis of dorsal hands, autoinflammatory syndromes (PAPA, PASH, SAPHO), rosacea fulminans/acne fulminans (overlap)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Acne fulminans (adolescent boys, trunk, systemic symptoms, comedones), acne conglobata, gram-negative folliculitis, halogenoderma (iodides/bromides), deep fungal infection, cutaneous TB, pyoderma gangrenosum, Sweet syndrome

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Oral prednisolone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day for 1–2 weeks to settle inflammation, then add oral isotretinoin 0.2–0.5 mg/kg/day for 3–4 months while tapering steroid
- Topical/intralesional steroids, gentle care, drainage of fluctuant nodules
- Pregnancy: oral steroids, azithromycin/erythromycin, topical metronidazole/azelaic acid; isotretinoin only after delivery (contraception)
- Treat underlying IBD

**Q7. How is it different from acne fulminans and acne conglobata?**
- Rosacea fulminans: young women, face only (central), sudden fluctuant nodules and sinus tracts with intense red/cyanotic background, no comedones, no systemic symptoms, no trunk
- Acne fulminans: adolescent males, trunk and face, ulcerative haemorrhagic nodules with fever, arthralgia, osteolytic bone lesions, raised ESR; acne conglobata: comedones (double), nodules, sinuses on trunk/face without systemic upset

**Q8. Histopathology.**
- Dense perifollicular and dermal neutrophilic abscesses with granulomatous inflammation, sinus tracts, without bacteria on culture (sterile)

**Q9. Pregnancy-related rosacea fulminans — management.**
- Commonly triggered in pregnancy; systemic steroids (prednisolone) + topical metronidazole/azelaic acid; erythromycin/azithromycin; isotretinoin only after delivery and lactation

## Quick spotter facts
- Explosive central facial nodules/abscesses on red background in a young woman, no comedones — rosacea fulminans
- Steroids first, then isotretinoin

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Rosacea). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
